detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, low sun from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot opens on an insert on the open mouth of the cylinder: a black circular cavity in the crusted end, the thin bright rim of the seam curving round it, the low sun flaring white along the top of the crust above it; only that object and what touches it is in frame. The camera is on the near lip of the pit looking down at the open end, a 135mm lens. The low sun comes from the LEFT across the crust. At the first frame the black circular cavity fills the CENTRE of the frame, half the frame's height. The shot is inside this place: The great raw crater on Horsell Common with the sun going down in 1894: walls of loose yellow sand and grey gravel dug back and scored by spades, a charred rim of blackened turf heaped with spoil, planks and pickaxes on the gravel floor, a broken length of new white railing trodden flat into the sand along the near lip. The camera tracks sideways to the left, a truck with small amplitude along the bright rim of the cavity, keeping the black mouth in the centre of frame as the flare of the low sun runs off the crust as the frame travels, the cavity comes round square to the lens and reads flat black, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 a thread of grey vapour lifts out of the mouth and drifts along the crust toward the seam, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:07 the camera is tracking through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
